s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Chief Minister in a hung Assembly:
1. The Constitution lays down detailed statutory criteria for the Governor to select the Chief Minister.
2. The Governor may exercise discretion in selecting a person to form the government.
3. An early floor test is ordinarily used to determine whether the government enjoys majority support.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: The Constitution does not prescribe detailed criteria for this situation, so statement 1 is false. The Governor may exercise discretion and an early floor test is used to establish majority support.
tq: Spot the absolute constitutional claim and retain the two practical features of a hung Assembly.
sec: ■ Chief Minister - appointment (Article 164), floor test, oath, non-member time limit, collective responsibility, salaries  [APPSC]

s: A Chief Minister continues in office constitutionally so long as he or she enjoys the confidence of the
x: The Chief Minister must retain the confidence of the Legislative Assembly. Loss of majority may lead to resignation or dismissal of the government after the position is established.
tq: Distinguish the formal pleasure of the Governor from the actual requirement of legislative confidence.
sec: ■ Chief Minister - appointment (Article 164), floor test, oath, non-member time limit, collective responsibility, salaries  [APPSC]

s: Who administers the oath of office and secrecy to the Chief Minister of a State?
o: The Chief Justice of the High Court
The Speaker of the Legislative Assembly
x: Under Article 164(3), the Governor administers the oath of office and secrecy to the Chief Minister and other ministers.
tq: Match the constitutional oath-taking function with the State-level appointing authority.
sec: ■ Chief Minister - appointment (Article 164), floor test, oath, non-member time limit, collective responsibility, salaries  [APPSC]

s: A person who is not a member of either House of the State Legislature may remain a Chief Minister or minister for a maximum period of
x: Article 164(4) permits a non-member to remain a minister, including Chief Minister, for six months. Thereafter, the person ceases to hold office unless elected to the State Legislature.
tq: Use the exact constitutional time limit rather than confusing it with the period for a legislative or parliamentary term.
sec: ■ Chief Minister - appointment (Article 164), floor test, oath, non-member time limit, collective responsibility, salaries  [APPSC]

s: A person elected to Parliament while holding a seat in a State Legislature must resign the State Legislature seat within how many days under the Prohibition of Simultaneous Membership Rules, 1950?
x: The person must resign the State Legislature seat within 14 days after being elected to Parliament under the stated rules.
tq: Discriminate between closely placed statutory time limits by focusing on the specific rule mentioned.
sec: ■ Chief Minister - appointment (Article 164), floor test, oath, non-member time limit, collective responsibility, salaries  [APPSC]

s: The salaries and allowances of ministers of a State are determined by the
x: Under Article 164(5), the salaries and allowances of State ministers are determined by the State Legislature by law.
tq: Identify the legislature that fixes ministerial remuneration instead of the authority that appoints ministers.
sec: ■ Chief Minister - appointment (Article 164), floor test, oath, non-member time limit, collective responsibility, salaries  [APPSC]

s:
Which of the following statements regarding the Chief Minister is correct?
1. The term of the Chief Minister is not fixed by the Constitution.
2. The Chief Minister recommends allocation of portfolios among ministers.
3. The Chief Minister may advise dissolution of the Legislative Assembly.
4. The Chief Minister has no role in the continuation or dropping of ministers.
x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 4 is false because the Chief Minister can recommend dropping ministers and has an important role in the composition of the Council.
tq: Reject the single reversal in an otherwise accurate list of Chief Ministerial functions.
sec: ■ Chief Minister - appointment (Article 164), floor test, oath, non-member time limit, collective responsibility, salaries  [APPSC]

s: The constitutional limit on the size of a State Council of Ministers, including the Chief Minister, was introduced through the
x: The 91st Constitutional Amendment Act, 2003 inserted Article 164(1A), which prescribes the upper and lower limits for the State Council of Ministers.
tq: Pair the constitutional provision with the amendment that inserted it, while separating it from the later tribal-welfare amendment.
sec: ■ Size of the State Council of Ministers - limits, amendment  [APPSC]

s: The Legislative Assembly of West Bengal has 294 seats. On applying the constitutional ceiling for the State Council of Ministers, the maximum number of ministers, including the Chief Minister, is
x: Fifteen per cent of 294 is 44.1; the applicable maximum is stated as 44 ministers. Thus, the Council cannot exceed 44 members including the Chief Minister.
tq: Apply the constitutional percentage ceiling to the Assembly strength and use the stated whole-number limit.
sec: ■ Size of the State Council of Ministers - limits, amendment  [APPSC]

s:
A minister for tribal welfare, who may also be entrusted with the welfare of Scheduled Castes and Backward Classes, is constitutionally required in which of the following States?
1. Chhattisgarh
2. Jharkhand
3. Madhya Pradesh
4. Odisha
x: The required tribal-welfare minister exists in all four States listed: Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, Madhya Pradesh and Odisha.
tq: Check every State in the constitutional list rather than assuming that only States with large tribal populations qualify.
sec: ■ Tribal welfare minister - Article 164(1) states  [APPSC]

s: The inclusion of Chhattisgarh and Jharkhand and the exclusion of Bihar from the constitutional requirement relating to a tribal-welfare minister were effected by the
x: The 94th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2006 made the relevant changes. Bihar was removed because it had no Scheduled Areas, while Chhattisgarh and Jharkhand were added.
tq: Separate the amendment dealing with tribal-welfare States from the amendment dealing with the size of the Council of Ministers.
sec: ■ Tribal welfare minister - Article 164(1) states  [APPSC]

s: Which one of the following is NOT a duty of the Chief Minister under Article 167 of the Constitution?
o: Furnishing information relating to administration and legislative proposals when called for by the Governor
Communicating decisions of the Council of Ministers to the Governor
Administering the oath of office to the Governor
Submitting for consideration of the Council of Ministers a matter decided by an individual minister, when required by the Governor
x: Administering the Governor's oath is not a duty of the Chief Minister under Article 167. The first three functions are constitutional duties of the Chief Minister.
tq: Find the one function outside Article 167 while retaining all three communication duties.
sec: ■ Duties of CM towards the Governor - Article 167  [other exams]

s:
Consider the following statements regarding Article 167:
1. The Chief Minister is the chief link between the Governor and the Council of Ministers.
2. The Chief Minister must communicate all decisions of the Council relating to administration and legislative proposals to the Governor.
3. The Governor may require the Chief Minister to place before the Council a matter decided by an individual minister.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: All three statements correctly describe the Chief Minister's duties and intermediary role under Article 167.
tq: When all listed statements directly express the constitutional link and information duties, select the complete combination.
sec: ■ Duties of CM towards the Governor - Article 167  [other exams]

s: Seeking information from the Chief Minister under Article 167 is regarded as a constitutional discretion of the
o: Chief Justice of the High Court
x: The Governor may call for information from the Chief Minister regarding administration and legislative proposals under Article 167.
tq: Match the information-seeking discretion with the constitutional office to which the duty is addressed.
sec: ■ Duties of CM towards the Governor - Article 167  [other exams]

s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Chief Ministerial position)
a. Chief Minister of Andhra State in 1953
a. Chief Minister of united Andhra Pradesh in 1956–1960
c. Chief Minister of residuary Andhra Pradesh in 2014

List-II (Person)
i. N. Chandrababu Naidu
ii. Neelam Sanjeeva Reddy
iii. Tanguturi Prakasam

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
x: Tanguturi Prakasam was the Chief Minister of Andhra State in 1953, Neelam Sanjeeva Reddy led united Andhra Pradesh in 1956–1960, and N. Chandrababu Naidu became Chief Minister of residuary Andhra Pradesh in 2014.
tq: Start with the sure historical pairing and then eliminate codes that disturb the remaining sequence.

s: The first Council of Ministers of united Andhra Pradesh in 1956 consisted of how many ministers?
x: The first cabinet of united Andhra Pradesh, formed in 1956 under Neelam Sanjeeva Reddy, had 13 ministers.
tq: Retain the precise numerical detail attached to the first cabinet rather than the later constitutional ceiling.
sec: ■ Chief Ministers - FIRST woman CM and AP FIRSTs  [other exams]

s: Who was the first Chief Minister of Andhra State, formed in 1953?
x: Tanguturi Prakasam was the first Chief Minister of Andhra State in 1953.
tq: Separate Andhra State in 1953 from united Andhra Pradesh formed in 1956.
sec: ■ Chief Ministers - FIRST woman CM and AP FIRSTs  [other exams]

s: The first Speaker of the Legislative Assembly of united Andhra Pradesh was
x: Nallapati Venkata Ramaiah was the first Speaker of the united Andhra Pradesh Legislative Assembly.
tq: Distinguish the first presiding officer of the Assembly from the first Chief Minister of the State.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Deputy Chief Minister in a State:
1. The office is expressly mentioned in the Constitution of India.
2. A Deputy Chief Minister is sworn in as a minister.
3. The post is generally a political arrangement.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: The Constitution does not specifically mention the office of Deputy Chief Minister, so statement 1 is false. The incumbent is sworn in as a minister and the office is a political arrangement.
tq: Reject the constitutional-status trap and retain the two facts describing the actual position.
sec: ■ Deputy Chief Minister - constitutional status, AP instances

s: In the order of precedence, a Deputy Chief Minister ranks with a
o: Union Minister of State at No. 10
x: A Deputy Chief Minister ranks with Union Ministers of State and occupies position No. 10 in the order of precedence.
tq: Use the paired rank and category together to avoid confusing the Deputy Chief Minister with a Cabinet Minister.
sec: ■ Deputy Chief Minister - constitutional status, AP instances

s: The Advocate General of a State must possess the qualifications required for appointment as a
o: Member of the State Public Service Commission
x: Article 165 requires the Advocate General to be qualified for appointment as a Judge of a High Court.
tq: Match the State constitutional law officer with the correct judicial qualification.
sec: ■ Advocate General - Article 165

s:
With reference to the Advocate General of a State, consider the following statements:
1. The Advocate General may speak and take part in the proceedings of either House of the State Legislature.
2. The Advocate General may take part in the proceedings of a committee of the State Legislature of which he or she is named a member.
3. The Advocate General has a right to vote in the proceedings in which he or she participates.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: Under Article 177, the Advocate General may speak and participate in the Legislature and its committees when entitled to do so, but has no right to vote. Therefore, statement 3 is false.
tq: Separate the right to participate from the distinct constitutional right to vote.
sec: ■ Advocate General - Article 165

s: In the order of precedence, the Advocate General of a State is placed at number
x: The Advocate General ranks at No. 25 in the order of precedence, below the Additional Solicitor General.
tq: Use the exact precedence number and compare it with the nearby rank of the Additional Solicitor General.
sec: ■ Advocate General - Article 165

s:
The 130th Constitution Amendment Bill, 2025 proposes amendments to which of the following Articles of the Constitution?
1. Article 75
2. Article 164
3. Article 239AA
4. Article 280
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
x: The Bill proposes amendments to Articles 75, 164 and 239AA. Article 280 is not included among the proposed amendments.
tq: Separate the relevant constitutional Articles from the unrelated Article 280.
sec: Universal angles

s: Under the 130th Constitution Amendment Bill, 2025, a Prime Minister, Chief Minister or Minister held in custody would be liable to removal on the 31st day when the custody is connected with an offence punishable with imprisonment of:
x: The proposed provision applies when the offence is punishable with imprisonment of five years or more and the person remains in custody for 30 consecutive days.
tq: Match the exact punishment threshold rather than choosing the more familiar seven- or ten-year figure.
sec: Universal angles

s: According to the 130th Constitution Amendment Bill, 2025, the relevant removal from office would take effect on:
x: The Bill proposes removal on the 31st day when the Prime Minister, Chief Minister or Minister has been held in custody for 30 consecutive days in the specified circumstances.
tq: Distinguish the qualifying period of 30 days from the day on which the consequence takes effect.
sec: Universal angles

s: The 130th Constitution Amendment Bill, 2025 was referred to which body for examination?
x: The 130th Constitution Amendment Bill, 2025 was referred to a Joint Parliamentary Committee for examination.
tq: Identify the parliamentary body entrusted with detailed examination of the Bill.
sec: Universal angles

s: Which one of the following statements correctly reflects the relationship between the Union and State Council of Ministers?
o: The Chief Minister mirrors the Speaker of the Lok Sabha in the State, with the corresponding provisions being Articles 93 and 94.
The Chief Minister mirrors the President in the State, with the corresponding provisions being Articles 153 and 154.
The Chief Minister mirrors the Vice-President in the State, with the corresponding provisions being Articles 63 and 64.
The Chief Minister mirrors the Prime Minister in the State, with the corresponding constitutional provisions being Articles 74 and 75 at the Union level.
x: The Chief Minister is the State-level counterpart of the Prime Minister in the parliamentary system. Articles 74 and 75 deal with the Union Council of Ministers headed by the Prime Minister.
tq: Use the institutional counterpart comparison and reject swaps with the President, Vice-President or Speaker.
sec: Universal angles

s: With reference to the constitutional arrangement of the States, which one of the following statements is correct?
o: Every State has a Vice-President as the counterpart of the Union Vice-President.
The State has no constitutional counterpart of the Vice-President.
The Governor is the constitutional counterpart of the Vice-President in every respect.
The Chief Minister performs the constitutional functions of the Vice-President in the State.
x: The State constitutional structure has no counterpart of the Vice-President. The Governor and Chief Minister occupy different constitutional positions and do not replace that office.
tq: Discriminate between an institutional counterpart and a merely similar constitutional office.
sec: Universal angles

s: In the West Bengal Assembly election held in May 2026, which one of the following combinations is correct?
o: BJP—175 seats out of 294; the defeated Chief Minister resigned immediately
BJP—207 seats out of 175; the defeated Chief Minister was appointed Governor
BJP—294 seats out of 207; the defeated Chief Minister dissolved the Assembly
BJP—207 seats out of 294; the defeated Chief Minister stated that she would not resign
x: The BJP won 207 of the 294 seats in West Bengal, while the defeated Chief Minister stated that she would not resign.
tq: Check both numerical components together and avoid options that reverse the seat total and seats won.
sec: Universal angles

s: The 11th meeting of the NITI Aayog Governing Council was notable because:
o: All Union Cabinet Ministers were made permanent members
All Governors of the States attended for the first time
The Council was converted into a constitutional body
All 28 Chief Ministers were present for the first time
x: The 11th NITI Aayog Governing Council saw the presence of all 28 Chief Ministers for the first time.
tq: Identify the distinctive participation fact instead of confusing Chief Ministers with Governors or Union Ministers.
sec: Universal angles

s: The Legislative Assembly of Andhra Pradesh has 175 seats. On the stated maximum-size rule for a State Council of Ministers, including the Chief Minister, the maximum number of ministers would be:
x: The stated maximum is 15 percent of the Assembly strength. Fifteen percent of 175 is 26.25, giving a maximum of 26 ministers when expressed as the applicable whole-number limit.
tq: Apply the percentage limit to the Assembly strength and use the applicable whole-number maximum.
sec: Universal angles
